reasoning: The extract sets out a monitoring plan for the passporting change. It says "We will monitor management information on the number of cases passported and passing or failing means tests", to be assessed "by different case types", and adds "We will also inspect information on appeals and complaints." It also promises to check for any disproportionate impact on protected groups, and it uses the consultation: "we have included some equalities questions in the consultation and will consider any responses and update this statement as necessary in due course." So there are named outcome measures, a plan for monitoring and a plan for using consultation responses. The lines carry no references. This reaches level 1 clearly. It is arguably level 2 on success measures and the monitoring process, but there is a gap. The extract gives no plan to test the policy first and no reason why testing would be inappropriate. It describes no evaluation as such, and gives no timetable. The line "We will monitor data where it is collected, although recognise that current collections are limited" admits that data may be insufficient. The strongest argument for level 2 is that the monitoring plan is fairly specific and the consultation is used. Against that, level 2 needs testing details or reasons why testing is inappropriate, and neither is shown. To reach level 2, the document would have to say whether the policy was tested or piloted, or why not, and set out a formal evaluation. For level 3 it would also have to give timing, explain the reasons for its approach, and commit to publishing the results.
